bibleSpine.kjv: And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father's name written in their foreheads. And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps: And they sung as it were a new song before the throne, and before the four beasts, and the elders: and no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth. These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins. These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb. And in their mouth was found no guile: for they are without fault before the throne of God.
bibleSpine.gloss: The 144,000 stand with the Lamb bearing the Father's name in their foreheads; the crowning trait of the last generation is that 'in their mouth was found no guile: for they are without fault before the throne of God' — the harvest of a perfectly reproduced character.

bibleSpine.kjv: The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.
bibleSpine.gloss: The Old Testament twin of Rev. 14:5: the sealed remnant shall not do iniquity, and no deceit is found in their mouth — what the gospel does, demonstrated in a people.

bibleSpine.kjv: Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints.
bibleSpine.gloss: The bride 'hath made herself ready' — the readiness is a granted arraying in the righteousness of saints; the church is presented complete, the harvest ripe for the marriage.

bibleSpine.kjv: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how. For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear. But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.
bibleSpine.gloss: The harvest law: first the blade, then the ear, then the full corn — 'when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.' The ripened likeness of Christ is the signal for the sickle.

bibleSpine.kjv: And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him that sat on the cloud, Thrust in thy sickle, and reap: for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe.
bibleSpine.gloss: The sickle is thrust in because 'the harvest of the earth is ripe' — the maturity of the grain (character) triggers the reaping; Christ comes when the crop is ready.

bibleSpine.kjv: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain. Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh.
bibleSpine.gloss: The Husbandman Himself waits with long patience 'for the precious fruit of the earth' through early and latter rain — Christ tarries for the ripened harvest of His character.

bibleSpine.kjv: To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,
bibleSpine.gloss: The purpose of the demonstration: through the church the manifold wisdom of God is made known to principalities and powers — the watching universe learns from the redeemed.

bibleSpine.kjv: And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night. And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.
bibleSpine.gloss: The accuser is answered and cast down: the saints 'overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony' — the vindication of God against Satan's charge is worked out in a people who prevail through Christ's blood.

bibleSpine.kjv: And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, Saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads. And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.
bibleSpine.gloss: The 144,000 are the sealed servants of God, marked in their foreheads before the winds of strife are loosed — the same company that stands faultless in Rev. 14, defined here as the sealed remnant.

bibleSpine.kjv: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy,
bibleSpine.gloss: The keeping and presenting is God's own act: He 'is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless' — the faultlessness of Rev. 14:5 is His power, not human merit.

bibleSpine.kjv: That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.
bibleSpine.gloss: The end of the harvest: a glorious church 'not having spot, or wrinkle... holy and without blemish' — the bride made ready, the ripened corn presented to the Lord.

bibleSpine.kjv: To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.
bibleSpine.gloss: The overcomer's victory is patterned on Christ's own — 'even as I also overcame' — the last generation overcomes in the same nature and by the same power, answering the accuser.

symbolDefs.meaning: The ripened likeness of Christ reproduced in His people — the maturing of character from blade to full corn — which is itself the signal for the sickle; when the fruit is fully brought forth Christ immediately reaps, so the ripeness of the crop, not an arbitrary date, sets the hour of His coming.
receipts: Mark 4:26-29 — first the blade, then the ear, then the full corn; 'when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come'
Revelation 14:15 — 'Thrust in thy sickle, and reap... for the harvest of the earth is ripe'
James 5:7-8 — the husbandman 'waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth' through the early and latter rain
Revelation 19:7-8 — the wife 'hath made herself ready,' arrayed in the righteousness of saints (the ripened, ready bride)

symbolDefs.meaning: The last generation — the sealed servants of God, redeemed from among men as firstfruits, who follow the Lamb whithersoever He goeth and in whose mouth is found no guile: they are without fault before the throne, the remnant of Israel that shall not do iniquity nor speak lies. In them the gospel's power is demonstrated and God is vindicated.
receipts: Revelation 14:1-5 — the hundred forty and four thousand with the Father's name in their foreheads; 'in their mouth was found no guile: for they are without fault before the throne of God'
Revelation 7:2-4 — sealed in their foreheads, 144,000 of the tribes of the children of Israel
Zephaniah 3:13 — 'The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth'
Ephesians 5:27 — presented a glorious church, holy and without blemish
Jude 1:24 — presented faultless before the presence of His glory

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: "When the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come." Christ is waiting with longing desire for the manifestation of Himself in His church. When the character of Christ shall be perfectly reproduced in His people, then He will come to claim them as His own.
witnesses.gloss: The keystone confirmation of the harvest law: the reproduced character of Christ IS the ripe fruit that triggers the sickle — Christ waits for the harvest of His own likeness, then comes. Directly on Mark 4:29.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: In their mouth was found no guile; for the soul temple had been so thoroughly cleansed before leaving earth that the human mouth became a channel for the words of God.... This will be the mind of those who are sealed. They are without fault; because Christ's righteousness covers them as a garment.... They overcame by the blood of the Lamb.
witnesses.gloss: A single passage confirming three of the section's own terms at once — 'no guile... without fault,' the sealed company, and 'overcame by the blood of the Lamb' — with Zephaniah 3:13 quoted in its own margin. The faultlessness is Christ's righteousness as a garment, not human merit.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The very image of God is to be reproduced in humanity. The honor of God, the honor of Christ, is involved in the perfection of the character of His people.
witnesses.gloss: The vindication motive stated plainly: God's own honor is staked on the perfection of character in His people — the manifold wisdom shown to the universe (Eph. 3:10) worked out in the last generation.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Christ has given His Spirit as a divine power to overcome all hereditary and cultivated tendencies to evil, and to impress His own character upon His church.
witnesses.gloss: How the harvest ripens: the Spirit overcomes every hereditary and cultivated tendency to evil and impresses Christ's character — tying the nature Christ took and the new birth to the completed victory of this section.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: In heaven Satan had declared that the sin of Adam revealed that human beings could not keep the law of God, and he sought to carry the universe with him in this belief.... Christ came to unmask the deceiver.... The Majesty of heaven would undertake the cause of man, and with the same facilities that man may obtain, stand the test and proving of God as man must stand it.
witnesses.gloss: The controversy this section resolves: Satan claimed the law could not be kept in human flesh; Christ answered it 'with the same facilities that man may obtain,' and the last generation repeats the demonstration — the accuser answered (Rev. 12:10-11).

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The last rays of merciful light, the last message of mercy to be given to the world, is a revelation of His character of love. The children of God are to manifest His glory. In their own life and character they are to reveal what the grace of God has done for them.
witnesses.gloss: The message and the demonstration are the same thing: the last message is a revelation of God's character, made visible in the life and character of His people — the harvest as the final proof of what grace can do.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Those who are living upon the earth when the intercession of Christ shall cease in the sanctuary above are to stand in the sight of a holy God without a mediator. Their robes must be spotless, their characters must be purified from sin by the blood of sprinkling.... This work is more clearly presented in the messages of Revelation 14.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the standing without a mediator and links it explicitly to the Revelation 14 harvest — spotless characters purified by the blood, the ripened company that stands after intercession ends.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: When He leaves the sanctuary, darkness covers the inhabitants of the earth. In that fearful time the righteous must live in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor.
witnesses.gloss: The setting of the final demonstration: the sealed remnant lives without an intercessor — the vindication is completed in a people kept faultless while no mediator pleads.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Just as soon as the people of God are sealed in their foreheads—it is not any seal or mark that can be seen, but a settling into the truth, both intellectually and spiritually, so they cannot be moved—just as soon as God's people are sealed and prepared for the shaking, it will come.
witnesses.gloss: Defines the sealing of Rev. 7:2-4 / 14:1 as a settling into truth so fixed the sealed cannot be moved — the inward reality behind the faultless standing of the 144,000.

witnesses.author: A. T. Jones
witnesses.quote: Perfection, perfection of character, is the Christian goal—perfection attained in human flesh in this world. Christ attained it in human flesh in this world and thus made and consecrated a way by which, in Him, every believer can attain it.
witnesses.gloss: The pioneer spine (Jones) for the whole section: character perfection is attainable in human flesh in this world because Christ attained it there first and consecrated the way — the ground of the last generation's faultlessness.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: God requires the entire surrender of the heart, before justification can take place; and in order for man to retain justification, there must be continual obedience, through active, living faith that works by love and purifies the soul.
witnesses.gloss: Ties righteousness by faith to actual obedience: justification is retained only through continual obedience by a faith that purifies the soul — so the harvest of a sinless people is the fruit of justification by faith, not a rival to it.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: It was in the order of God that Christ should take upon himself the form and nature of fallen man, that he might be made perfect through suffering, and himself endure the strength of Satan's fierce temptations.
witnesses.gloss: Anchors the tie-back the section gathers: Christ took the nature of fallen man and overcame in it — the same nature in which the last generation now demonstrates complete victory, closing the chain from the nature Christ took to the harvest.

historyAnchor: The harvest/vindication theme was crystallized in Seventh-day Adventism at and after the 1888 Minneapolis General Conference, when A. T. Jones and E. J. Waggoner's righteousness-by-faith message reframed the perfecting of the last generation, and Ellen White's Christ's Object Lessons (1900) fixed the COL 69 statement as its classic expression.
uncertainties: The Waggoner works named in the source map (Christ and His Righteousness / CHR, Waggoner on Romans / WOR) did not surface by title or content search in this local corpus; no Waggoner refcode could be verified, so none is cited — the pioneer voice is carried by the verified A. T. Jones anchor (CWCP 84.1). If Waggoner corroboration is required, it should be pulled from a corpus where CHR/WOR resolve.

Several EGW passages exist in multiple parallel editions (e.g., the 'character perfectly reproduced' statement appears at COL 69.1, CT 324.3, LDE 39.2, LHU 274.6, SD 32.7, Mar 112.6); COL 69.1 is cited as the primary/original source per the section scope, with the others available as parallels.
